items.text: How to get ahead of the job-search 'cattle call'
items.article: Career coaches say job seekers should build relationships at target companies before a role is posted — not wait to apply online. The best way to beat the line for a job is to get there before it forms. Talking with an employer before the company ever posts a job — and not after — could help you land a role there, said veteran career coach Laura Labovich. She recommends that job seekers identify where they want to work, examine their network for any ties to the organization, and start building relationships inside well before a job post goes up. "The way to win is to not apply. Get in before they have the opening. Make connections. Become an insider," Labovich said. If you wait until you see a job post before reaching out to an employer, you might already be too late, she said. That's because once a role is posted, recruiters or HR will often feel compelled to tell you to apply online — even if they already know you — to ensure that every candidate gets equal consideration, Labovich said. Getting in line with everybody else can make the process seem "more like a cattle call," she said.
